# Validation Report: Elevator Predictive Maintenance Retrofit Vibration Sensors (Provisional)

## Summary
This Provisional evaluation yields a verdict of **NEEDS_WORK** (decision reason: `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`) with a composite score of **3.2** and **LOW** confidence (**0.16**). Although basic building predictive maintenance and AI fault detection solutions exist in the commercial landscape, market sources fail to identify specific buyer segments or validate willingness-to-pay/pricing, triggering a fatal floor (`FLOOR_NO_MARKET`). Additionally, no community sentiment data was returned, and feasibility evidence remains partial for full-pipeline production elevator deployment.

## Scope
- **Startup Idea**: A subscription service that fits retrofit vibration sensors to commercial building lifts and warns facilities managers of bearing wear weeks before a breakdown, replacing the fixed quarterly inspection contracts most landlords buy today.
- **Category**: Commercial elevator predictive maintenance IoT
- **Target User**: Commercial facilities managers and building operations directors
- **Problem**: Scheduled periodic inspections fail to detect mechanical bearing degradation between visits, leading to sudden elevator breakdowns and costly emergency downtime.
- **Technology Claim**: Retrofit non-invasive vibration sensors paired with anomaly detection algorithms can detect mechanical bearing wear weeks prior to failure without tapping into proprietary OEM elevator controllers.
- **As of Date**: 2026-09-06

## Five-Score Rubric
- **Demand (D)**: **1/5** (Evidence Thin)
  - *Anchor*: Evidence does not reach this question — the sentiment branch returned fewer than 5 usable threads and no problem thread.
- **Market (M)**: **0/5**
  - *Anchor*: At least 3 market sources, and none of them names a buyer segment for this problem, and none states a price or a budget anyone spends on it. Evaluated via [OXMaint](https://oxmaint.com/industries/property-management/elevator-predictive-maintenance-ai-fault-detection), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/from-reactive-predictive-future-elevator-maintenance-india-pmknf), and [Wattsense](https://www.wattsense.com/blog/building-management/examples-of-predictive-maintenance/).
- **Competitive Room (C)**: **2/5** (Evidence Thin)
  - *Anchor*: No source states an axis of beatability, and either no competitor is named or at least 1 named competitor is not shown to be vendor owned. Named competitors include [OXMaint](https://oxmaint.com/industries/property-management/elevator-predictive-maintenance-ai-fault-detection) and [Wattsense](https://www.wattsense.com/blog/building-management/examples-of-predictive-maintenance/).
- **Feasibility (F)**: **3/5** (Evidence Thin)
  - *Anchor*: At least 1 repository in the feasibility evidence is reusable: marked SOLVES_ENTIRELY or PARTIAL, licensed for commercial use, and pushed within 12 months ([holden-mcgorin/UniPHM](https://github.com/holden-mcgorin/UniPHM)).
- **Headroom Over Free (X)**: **3/5** (Evidence Thin)
  - *Anchor*: No free substitute repository exists, and free coverage is unsettled or settled at no more than a separable part of the core job. Evaluated against [OXMaint](https://oxmaint.com/industries/property-management/elevator-predictive-maintenance-ai-fault-detection) and [Wattsense](https://www.wattsense.com/blog/building-management/examples-of-predictive-maintenance/).

## Verdict & Confidence
- **Verdict**: `NEEDS_WORK`
- **Decision Reason**: `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`
- **Confidence**: `0.16` (Band: `LOW`)
- **Provisional**: `true`

## Evidence Gaps
- The sentiment branch returned an empty result status (`0 results found`) for query 'elevator predictive maintenance', resulting in an evidence gap regarding direct user statements about bearing wear, emergency breakdowns, or sensor retrofits.
- Lack of production-ready, commercially licensed end-to-end IoT sensor pipelines specifically tailored for commercial elevator machinery vibration analysis.
- Uncertainty regarding signal-to-noise ratio handling across diverse legacy elevator makes and models without proprietary controller integration.
- Jurisdictional legal mandates dictating minimum human elevator inspection frequencies irrespective of continuous digital condition monitoring.
- Liability allocation between the sensor subscription provider, building owner, and maintenance technicians in the event of an undetected mechanical failure.

## Risks
- **Fatal Floor Violation**: Triggered `FLOOR_NO_MARKET` because zero market sources state buyer pricing, budget, or distinct paying segments.
- **Thin Dimensions**: Demand (D), Competitive Room (C), Feasibility (F), and Headroom Over Free (X) are all flagged as evidence thin.
- **Failed/Empty Sentiment Branch**: Tool status was `empty` for sentiment retrieval, leaving customer pain and replacement willingness completely unsubstantiated.
- **Commercial Licensing & Maintenance Hazards**:
  - [zhangxiaoling/Bearing-fault-detection](https://github.com/zhangxiaoling/Bearing-fault-detection) does not permit commercial use and has not been pushed to in 89 months.
  - [wargod797/Fault_diagnosis_ballbearing_wavelet](https://github.com/wargod797/Fault_diagnosis_ballbearing_wavelet) does not permit commercial use and has not been pushed to in 74 months.
  - [LGDiMaggio/predictive-maintenance-mcp](https://github.com/LGDiMaggio/predictive-maintenance-mcp) does not permit commercial use and was determined to be irrelevant.
  - Only [holden-mcgorin/UniPHM](https://github.com/holden-mcgorin/UniPHM) offers a commercial license and recent commits, but only partially addresses the technical problem.

## Kill Criteria
- Commercial elevator insurers or statutory safety regulators mandate fixed quarterly on-site physical technician inspections regardless of remote continuous IoT monitoring.
- Third-party retrofit magnetic vibration sensors attached to lift motor bearings fail to detect standard spalling/pitting degradation with >80% accuracy without access to proprietary OEM controller data.
- Incumbent elevator maintenance providers explicitly void equipment service warranties when third-party IoT hardware is affixed to elevator hoisting machinery.

## Cheapest Next Test
Interview 10 commercial facilities managers to determine if insurance or local municipal elevator safety codes permit replacing scheduled human quarterly inspections with continuous vibration monitoring.
